title: SailPoint Admin Domain 7 questions (7.1, 7.2, 7.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A new administrator asks what a source represents in Identity Security Cloud. Which answer is BEST?
choices: A group of identities that share an identity profile
A bundle of entitlements that users can request together
A saved search that returns all identities from a single department or business unit
The ISC representation of a system that keeps its own accounts or personnel records
questions.answer: The ISC representation of a system that keeps its own accounts or personnel records
questions.explanation: A source represents an application, database or directory with its own accounts, and connectors load those accounts and access into ISC. A bundle of requestable entitlements is an access profile.

questions.stem: An auditor asks why every application must be connected as a source before ISC can govern it. Which reason is MOST accurate?
choices: ISC can only govern accounts and access it has loaded from a source
Sources replace the application's own sign-in page
Sources are required to create lifecycle states
Sources encrypt the application's database at rest using the tenant's keys
questions.answer: ISC can only govern accounts and access it has loaded from a source
questions.explanation: Governance acts on aggregated accounts and entitlements, so an unconnected system is invisible to campaigns and requests. Sources do not encrypt target data or replace sign-in.

questions.stem: A flat file source has no connector that can make changes. When an access request is approved for it, who is notified to make the change?
choices: The identity's manager, through a certification
The SoD violation owner, through MySailPoint
The Helpdesk user level, through a source banner
The source owner, through a task in their Task Manager
questions.answer: The source owner, through a task in their Task Manager
questions.explanation: For flat file sources, source owners receive Task Manager notifications when accounts must be added, changed or removed. Certifications and banners do not carry provisioning work.

questions.stem: An admin finishes configuring a new source but skips the Source Owner field. Which problem is MOST likely to follow?
choices: Its accounts can no longer be correlated to identities
Its virtual appliance cluster stops responding
Source owner certification campaigns for it show an error
The source cannot be aggregated until an owner is set
questions.answer: Source owner certification campaigns for it show an error
questions.explanation: Without a source owner, source owner campaigns error and approvals that include the source owner escalate to an admin. Aggregation and correlation still work.

questions.stem: An access request's approval scheme includes the source owner, but the source has no owner assigned. What happens to that approval step?
choices: It is escalated to an Admin
It is skipped and the request is provisioned
It is sent to the requester's manager instead
It is cancelled and the requester is notified
questions.answer: It is escalated to an Admin
questions.explanation: Documentation states that when the source owner is in the approval scheme and none is set, approvals escalate to an Admin. That is why assigning owners is part of source setup.

questions.stem: A security lead wants a team to manage one source and its access without receiving full Admin rights. Which source setting supports this?
choices: The Governance Group for Source Management
The Percentage of Deleted Accounts Allowed
The Account Correlation configuration
The delta aggregation setting
questions.answer: The Governance Group for Source Management
questions.explanation: The source's governance group grants source sub-admin oversight of that source and its access. Correlation, deletion thresholds and delta settings control data loading.

questions.stem: Before saving a newly configured direct connect source, an admin wants to confirm ISC can reach the target with the supplied credentials. What should the admin use?
choices: Download Correlation File in Uncorrelated Accounts
Test Connection in the Review and Test section
Export on the source's Accounts list
Download Account Schema in Account Aggregation
questions.answer: Test Connection in the Review and Test section
questions.explanation: Test Connection checks connectivity and credentials before aggregation. The schema and correlation downloads are templates for files, and Export lists existing accounts.

questions.stem: An HR system feeds employee records that should create identities in ISC. How should the admin use this source?
choices: Attach it as List A of an SoD policy
Add it to a password sync group
Make it the authoritative source of an identity profile
Leave it non-authoritative and correlate its accounts later
questions.answer: Make it the authoritative source of an identity profile
questions.explanation: Identity profiles are built on an authoritative source, and its accounts create identities. Non-authoritative sources only correlate accounts to identities that already exist.

questions.stem: Accounts are aggregated from a non-authoritative application source. What happens to an account that matches no identity?
choices: It is deleted at the end of the aggregation
It stays uncorrelated rather than creating a new identity
It creates a new identity in the default identity profile
It becomes the owner of the source
questions.answer: It stays uncorrelated rather than creating a new identity
questions.explanation: Only authoritative sources create identities. Unmatched accounts on other sources stay uncorrelated until correlation logic or a manual link assigns them.

questions.stem: Contractors exist in a contractor database and employees in HR, and some people appear in both. What controls which source's identity profile an identity uses?
choices: The priority set on the identity profiles
The source with the most recent aggregation
The order in which the sources were created
The alphabetical order of the source names
questions.answer: The priority set on the identity profiles
questions.explanation: When an identity has accounts on several authoritative sources, profile priority decides which profile applies. Creation order and aggregation time do not.

questions.stem: An admin plans to change an authoritative source's configuration. Which identity data depends MOST directly on that source?
choices: Identity attributes mapped from its accounts in the identity profile
The entitlements aggregated from unrelated directories
The passwords stored on other non-authoritative sources in the same sync group
The SoD policies' risk levels
questions.answer: Identity attributes mapped from its accounts in the identity profile
questions.explanation: Identity profile mappings read attributes from the authoritative source's accounts, so changes ripple into identity attributes. Other sources' data and policy levels are independent.

questions.stem: An identity's only authoritative account disappears from HR, but the identity also has an account on a lower-priority authoritative contractor source. What does ISC do?
choices: Deletes the identity immediately during aggregation
Marks the identity as an SoD violation
Moves it to the contractor identity profile and recalculates its attributes
Keeps the identity in the HR profile but blanks every attribute mapped from HR
questions.answer: Moves it to the contractor identity profile and recalculates its attributes
questions.explanation: When the higher-priority authoritative account is deleted, the identity moves to the next authoritative profile and its attributes are recalculated from that profile's mappings.

questions.stem: A team asks whether an Active Directory source should be authoritative. Which statement BEST reflects common practice?
choices: AD is usually non-authoritative, with HR authoritative
AD must always be the only authoritative source
Every source in a tenant must be authoritative
AD can be connected only if it is marked authoritative
questions.answer: AD is usually non-authoritative, with HR authoritative
questions.explanation: Treating HR as the authoritative source and correlating AD accounts to those identities is common practice, not a product rule: ISC lets any source, AD included, be authoritative when an identity profile is built on it. Nothing forces every source, or AD, to be authoritative.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes a direct connection to a source?
choices: An admin uploads a .csv file of accounts by hand
Users sign in to the source through ISC single sign-on
Approvers receive a ticket for each change
ISC reads changes from the system itself
questions.answer: ISC reads changes from the system itself
questions.explanation: A direct connection uses connection details so ISC can read accounts, and often provision, without file uploads. A flat file connection relies on an imported file.

questions.stem: A legacy payroll application has no API and cannot be reached from the network. How can ISC still govern its accounts?
choices: Configure a SaaS connector with no credentials
Enable delta aggregation on its source
Add the application to a password sync group
Configure a flat file source and import exported account files
questions.answer: Configure a flat file source and import exported account files
questions.explanation: Flat file sources load accounts from a file such as a .csv, which suits disconnected systems. Sync groups and delta aggregation need a direct connection.

questions.stem: An admin sets up a flat file source for a disconnected app. Which statement about it is accurate?
choices: It requires an IQService host to import files
It can reset user passwords through Password Manager
It provisions accounts directly once a VA is attached
It is read only, so changes are made manually
questions.answer: It is read only, so changes are made manually
questions.explanation: File-based sources are disconnected and read only, so provisioning becomes manual tasks for owners. They cannot reset passwords or provision directly.

questions.stem: An admin needs a template showing the columns a flat file source expects. Where is it obtained?
choices: Export on the Policy Violations page
Download Correlation File on the Uncorrelated Accounts page
Generate the Uncorrelated Accounts report
Download Account Schema on Account Aggregation
questions.answer: Download Account Schema on Account Aggregation
questions.explanation: Download Account Schema gives a template matching the source's attributes. The correlation file lists uncorrelated accounts for manual linking.

questions.stem: A delimited file lists one row per account-entitlement pair. After import, each account shows only one entitlement. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Delta aggregation is disabled
The file is not sorted by account ID
The source has no source owner
The file is larger than the recommended size
questions.answer: The file is not sorted by account ID
questions.explanation: Documentation advises sorting a delimited file by account ID so multiple rows for one account merge. Owner and delta settings do not affect row grouping.

questions.stem: An admin has already uploaded this week's accounts file but needs to rerun the same import after fixing correlation. Which option avoids uploading again?
choices: Aggregate Using Latest File
Start Aggregation
Test Connection
Download Account Schema
questions.answer: Aggregate Using Latest File
questions.explanation: Flat file sources offer Aggregate Using Latest File to reuse the previously uploaded list. Start Aggregation and Test Connection apply to direct connections.

questions.stem: In the sources list, an admin filters by Connection type. Which two connection types will the admin see?
choices: Authoritative and non-authoritative
Preventive and detective
Direct connection and flat file
Optimized and unoptimized
questions.answer: Direct connection and flat file
questions.explanation: Connection type describes how ISC gets data: a direct connection or an imported flat file. Authoritative status and optimization are separate settings.

questions.stem: An on-premises Active Directory forest must be connected to ISC. What does the VA-based connector require?
choices: A SAML trust between ISC and the domain controllers
No local components at all, because all connectors run in the SailPoint cloud
A virtual appliance cluster on the network that can reach the directory
A flat file uploaded to the source each night
questions.answer: A virtual appliance cluster on the network that can reach the directory
questions.explanation: VA-based connectors run through an on-premises virtual appliance cluster that communicates with ISC and the target. SAML handles authentication, not connector traffic.

questions.stem: A team wants to connect a cloud SaaS application without deploying any on-premises components. Which connector style fits BEST?
choices: A SaaS connector
A SAML Just-in-Time provisioning source
A file-based connector with nightly uploads
A VA-based connector
questions.answer: A SaaS connector
questions.explanation: SaaS connectors read and provision without an on-premises VA cluster. File-based connectors need manual files, and JIT sources create accounts at first sign-in.

questions.stem: A manager asks what a Quick Compliance connector provides compared with a deep governance connector. Which answer is accurate?
choices: Direct database replication of identity attributes
Read-only aggregation with minimal setup
Automatic SoD blocking for the source's entitlements
Full provisioning and password management on the source
questions.answer: Read-only aggregation with minimal setup
questions.explanation: Quick Compliance connectors support aggregation only, which suits visibility and certification. Deep governance connectors add provisioning, schema configuration and password settings.

questions.stem: A source page shows the banner VA cluster failing. What should the admin check FIRST?
choices: That the SoD policy has items in both lists
That the identity profile priority is correct
That the VA cluster for the source is running, online and visible
That the source owner has accepted ownership of the source in Task Manager
questions.answer: That the VA cluster for the source is running, online and visible
questions.explanation: This banner means the virtual appliance serving the source is down or having problems. Ownership, priority and SoD settings do not cause it.

questions.stem: An older document refers to VA-based connectors by a different name. Which earlier term did SailPoint use for them?
choices: Multi-host sources
Flat file sources
Quick Compliance sources
Direct sources
questions.answer: Direct sources
questions.explanation: SailPoint documentation notes that VA-based connectors were previously referred to as direct sources. Flat file and Quick Compliance are different connector categories.

questions.stem: An identity provider is configured to create accounts in an app the first time users sign in. Which ISC source type relates to this?
choices: A JDBC source with delta aggregation
A delimited file source
A SCIM 2.0 source with no credentials
A SAML Just-in-Time provisioning source
questions.answer: A SAML Just-in-Time provisioning source
questions.explanation: A SAML JIT provisioning source connects with the identity provider to create an app account at first authentication. The other types aggregate from files or databases.

questions.stem: An admin must onboard dozens of similar Microsoft SQL Server instances at once rather than one source at a time. Which ISC feature supports this?
choices: Password sync groups for bulk password changes
Multi-Host groups for bulk source creation
Governance groups for source management
Search subscriptions for scheduled reports
questions.answer: Multi-Host groups for bulk source creation
questions.explanation: Multi-Host groups create sources in bulk for infrastructure components. Sync groups, governance groups and subscriptions solve different problems.

questions.stem: A custom in-house application stores its users and roles in a SQL database. Which generic connector is the BEST fit?
choices: Delimited File
LDAP
JDBC
SCIM 2.0
questions.answer: JDBC
questions.explanation: The JDBC connector reads and writes database tables with SQL. SCIM needs a SCIM API, and LDAP targets directory servers.

questions.stem: A cloud app exposes REST endpoints for users and groups but no standard provisioning protocol. Which generic connector should the admin consider?
choices: JDBC
Delimited File
Web Services
LDAP
questions.answer: Web Services
questions.explanation: The Web Services connector calls an application's REST or SOAP endpoints for accounts and groups. JDBC needs database access and LDAP needs a directory.

questions.stem: A vendor's app supports the standard System for Cross-domain Identity Management protocol. Which connector requires the LEAST custom configuration?
choices: Web Services
SCIM 2.0
JDBC
Delimited File
questions.answer: SCIM 2.0
questions.explanation: The SCIM 2.0 connector uses the standard user and group endpoints, so little mapping is needed. Web Services would require defining each endpoint yourself.

questions.stem: An on-premises directory server that is not Active Directory needs to be governed. Which generic connector fits BEST?
choices: Delimited File
LDAP
Web Services
SCIM 2.0
questions.answer: LDAP
questions.explanation: The LDAP connector reads and provisions standard directory objects. SCIM and Web Services target web APIs, and a delimited file would be read only.

questions.stem: A small business app can only export a .csv list of its users and their groups. Which connector should the admin use?
choices: JDBC
Delimited File
SCIM 2.0
LDAP
questions.answer: Delimited File
questions.explanation: The Delimited File connector imports exported .csv data into a read-only source. The others need live connectivity the app does not offer.

questions.stem: A project manager asks why the team chose a generic connector instead of a dedicated one for an obscure app. Which reason is MOST valid?
choices: Generic connectors make every source authoritative
No dedicated connector exists, but the app speaks SQL, LDAP or SCIM
Generic connectors skip the need for a source owner
Generic connectors never need credentials or a VA
questions.answer: No dedicated connector exists, but the app speaks SQL, LDAP or SCIM
questions.explanation: Generic connectors cover apps that use standard protocols when SailPoint has no app-specific connector. Ownership, authority and credentials still apply.

questions.stem: Which generic connector types typically require a virtual appliance because they reach systems inside the corporate network?
choices: JDBC and LDAP against on-premises servers
Quick Compliance SaaS connectors
SAML Just-in-Time sources created at sign-in
Delimited File imports uploaded through the browser
questions.answer: JDBC and LDAP against on-premises servers
questions.explanation: On-premises databases and directories are reached through a VA cluster. File uploads and SaaS connectors do not need one.

questions.stem: Match each generic connector to the system it suits.

pairs.match: A custom app storing users in a SQL database
A SaaS app with standard user and group endpoints
An app with custom REST or SOAP endpoints
A disconnected app that exports .csv lists

targets_extra: A mainframe reached only by terminal screen scraping
questions.explanation: Each generic connector matches a standard way of reaching account data: SQL, LDAP, SCIM, custom web APIs or exported files. None of them is a screen-scraping tool.

questions.stem: An admin is choosing a flat file source for a disconnected app. Which TWO statements about it are true?
choices: Account data is loaded by uploading a file such as a .csv
It requires a virtual appliance cluster to read the file
Changes are fulfilled manually, with tasks for the source owner
It can join a password sync group
It supports delta aggregation of changed accounts
answers: Account data is loaded by uploading a file such as a .csv
Changes are fulfilled manually, with tasks for the source owner
questions.explanation: Flat file sources are read only and loaded from imported files, so changes become manual tasks. Sync groups and delta aggregation need direct connections, and no VA is needed to upload a file.

questions.stem: Put the steps for onboarding a new direct connect source in order.
items: Create the source and enter its connection details
Select Test Connection to confirm connectivity
questions.explanation: Connection details are tested before use, an owner is set, and correlation is configured before the first aggregation so accounts link to identities on first load.

questions.stem: An admin explains aggregation to a new analyst. Which description is BEST?
choices: Combining several identity profiles into one
Merging duplicate identities after correlation
Pushing identity attribute changes out to every connected source
Loading accounts and their access from a source into ISC
questions.answer: Loading accounts and their access from a source into ISC
questions.explanation: Aggregation reads accounts and access from the source system into ISC. Pushing changes out is provisioning or attribute sync.

questions.stem: Accounts show group names after account aggregation, but the groups have no descriptions or owners in ISC. Which task should the admin run?
choices: A manual correlation file upload
Another optimized account aggregation
Entitlement aggregation for the source
A Test Connection on the source
questions.answer: Entitlement aggregation for the source
questions.explanation: Account aggregation loads accounts and the entitlement values they hold, while entitlement aggregation loads the entitlement objects and their details. Correlation and connection tests do not load groups.

questions.stem: An admin wants to build access profiles from Active Directory groups that nobody currently belongs to. Which aggregation makes those groups available?
choices: Entitlement aggregation
Delta account aggregation
Account aggregation with optimization
Single-account aggregation
questions.answer: Entitlement aggregation
questions.explanation: Entitlement aggregation reads the group catalog itself, including empty groups. Account aggregations only reveal entitlements that accounts hold.

questions.stem: A Helpdesk user needs the current locked status of one user's account without loading the whole source. What should they do?
choices: Reset the source using the API
Use Aggregate Account on that account
Start a full source aggregation
Upload a new correlation file
questions.answer: Use Aggregate Account on that account
questions.explanation: Single-account aggregation refreshes one account's data and status. A full aggregation or reset is heavier and unnecessary for one account.

questions.stem: After aggregating a single account, the admin notices the identity's attributes have not changed. Why?
choices: It only works on flat file sources
Identity attributes update only after a source reset
The source owner must approve the new values first
It updates account data but not identity attributes
questions.answer: It updates account data but not identity attributes
questions.explanation: Aggregating one account updates its account data but does not recalculate identity attributes or trigger provisioning. A later identity refresh handles that.

questions.stem: A data owner asks which account information ISC obtains during account aggregation. Which answer is MOST complete?
choices: Only the passwords, so that password policies can be checked
Schema attributes for each account, including the entitlements it holds
Only accounts that already correlate to an identity
Only the account names, with attributes loaded later by identity refresh
questions.answer: Schema attributes for each account, including the entitlements it holds
questions.explanation: Account aggregation reads attributes defined in the account schema, including multi-valued entitlement attributes. It never collects passwords and also loads uncorrelated accounts.

questions.stem: An admin aggregates a flat file source of accounts and then uploads a separate file of groups. Why is the second file needed?
choices: Entitlement details come from their own entitlement import
Accounts cannot be correlated to identities without the group file
Deletes are only processed from the group file
The source cannot have an owner without it
questions.answer: Entitlement details come from their own entitlement import
questions.explanation: Flat file sources take accounts and entitlements as separate imports, matching account and entitlement aggregation. Correlation and ownership do not depend on the entitlement file.

questions.stem: Which aggregation type is the default in ISC?
choices: Unoptimized aggregation
Optimized aggregation
Delta aggregation
Single-account aggregation
questions.answer: Optimized aggregation
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation is the default and skips records that have not changed. Unoptimized and delta aggregations are chosen deliberately.

questions.stem: During an optimized aggregation, an account exists and none of its data changed. How is it processed?
choices: It is re-correlated against every identity attribute
It is flagged as uncorrelated until reviewed
It is deleted and recreated to refresh its data
It is skipped, and correlation is not evaluated again
questions.answer: It is skipped, and correlation is not evaluated again
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation reads every record but skips unchanged accounts, so correlation and manager correlation are not re-run for them. That is why correlation changes need an unoptimized run.

questions.stem: An admin changed a source's correlation configuration, but previously uncorrelated accounts with unchanged data are still uncorrelated after the nightly aggregation. What should the admin do?
choices: Run another optimized aggregation from the UI
Run an unoptimized aggregation so unchanged accounts are re-evaluated
Delete the source and recreate it
Enable delta aggregation and wait for the next scheduled run to pick them up
questions.answer: Run an unoptimized aggregation so unchanged accounts are re-evaluated
questions.explanation: Optimized runs skip unchanged accounts, so new correlation logic never reaches them. An unoptimized aggregation reprocesses every account and re-evaluates correlation.

questions.stem: How does an admin run an unoptimized aggregation on a direct connect source?
choices: Call the load-accounts API with disableOptimization set to true
Select Start Aggregation twice in the UI
Turn on delta aggregation in the source's Aggregation Settings page
Enable Account Deletion before aggregating
questions.answer: Call the load-accounts API with disableOptimization set to true
questions.explanation: The load-accounts API accepts disableOptimization=true for that one run. Scheduled and manual UI aggregations always run optimized.

questions.stem: An admin set disableOptimization to true on one API aggregation. What happens on the next scheduled aggregation?
choices: It fails until the source is reset
It stays unoptimized until the flag is reset
It runs optimized again, because the flag applies only to that call
It switches to delta aggregation automatically for all later scheduled runs
questions.answer: It runs optimized again, because the flag applies only to that call
questions.explanation: The flag affects only the aggregation it was sent with. Later API runs need it again, and UI or scheduled runs are always optimized.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes delta aggregation?
choices: It loads every account on the source and recalculates correlation for each one
It loads entitlements but never accounts
It loads only new or changed accounts since the last run, on supported sources
It compares two identity profiles and merges their identities
questions.answer: It loads only new or changed accounts since the last run, on supported sources
questions.explanation: Delta aggregation reduces load by reading only changes, and only some connectors support it. Rechecking every account describes an unoptimized run.

questions.stem: Active Directory uses delta aggregation, and the team just moved many users to new OUs. What should the admin do?
choices: Reset the source and delete its access profiles
Disable correlation until the next delta run
Keep running delta aggregations, because delta handles OU moves natively
Run a full account aggregation, because delta does not support OU moves
questions.answer: Run a full account aggregation, because delta does not support OU moves
questions.explanation: Documentation warns that delta aggregation does not support OU moves and can create duplicate accounts. A full aggregation avoids that.

questions.stem: Which of these connectors supports delta aggregation in ISC?
choices: Microsoft Active Directory
Generic Flat File
Any source with an owner
Delimited File
questions.answer: Microsoft Active Directory
questions.explanation: Active Directory is on the supported list, along with JDBC, Workday and others. File-based sources load whole files and do not do delta.

questions.stem: An admin wants an HR source aggregated every day at 2 AM. Where is this configured?
choices: On the source's Account Aggregation page, using Enable Schedule
In the Aggregation Activity list
On the identity profile page, using the identity refresh schedule
On the SoD policy's Schedule action
questions.answer: On the source's Account Aggregation page, using Enable Schedule
questions.explanation: Account aggregation schedules are set on the source, with frequency and start time. SoD schedules evaluate policies, and Aggregation Activity only shows history.

questions.stem: A schedule starts at 2 PM and recurs every 8 hours. How many aggregations run each day?
choices: Unlimited, until an admin cancels the schedule
One, because recurrences need a monthly schedule
Two, at 2 PM and 10 PM
Three, at 2 PM, 10 PM and 6 AM
questions.answer: Two, at 2 PM and 10 PM
questions.explanation: Recurring daily schedules start at the chosen time and stop at midnight. A 2 PM start every 8 hours gives runs at 2 PM and 10 PM.

questions.stem: An admin notices scheduled aggregations shift by an hour from local time after daylight saving starts. Why?
choices: Schedules follow the source owner's time zone
Schedules use the VA cluster's GMT offset and do not shift for daylight saving
Schedules follow the time zone set in the admin's browser when the schedule was saved
Schedules drift because delta aggregation is enabled
questions.answer: Schedules use the VA cluster's GMT offset and do not shift for daylight saving
questions.explanation: Aggregation schedule time comes from the connected VA cluster's time zone as a GMT offset, so standard time is always used. Browser and owner time zones do not apply.

questions.stem: An admin wants a monthly aggregation on the 31st. What will the scheduler allow?
choices: Only the last day of the month
Only the first Monday of the month
Only dates from the 1st to the 28th
Any date, skipping months without that day
questions.answer: Only dates from the 1st to the 28th
questions.explanation: Monthly aggregations can be set on any date from 1 to 28, so they run every month.

questions.stem: An aggregation started by mistake against a slow target system. How can the admin stop it?
choices: Cancel it from the aggregation card or the Aggregation History page
Disable the identity profile
Delete the source while the aggregation runs, which stops the job at once
Restart the browser session
questions.answer: Cancel it from the aggregation card or the Aggregation History page
questions.explanation: In-progress aggregations can be cancelled from the source's aggregation card menu or terminated from Aggregation History. A source cannot be deleted while it is in use.

questions.stem: Leadership wants to see all aggregations across sources from the last 90 days. Where should the admin look?
choices: Admin > Password Mgmt > Sync Groups
Admin > Connections > Aggregation Activity
Admin > SoD Policies > Policy Violations
Admin > Global > System Settings
questions.answer: Admin > Connections > Aggregation Activity
questions.explanation: Aggregation Activity shows aggregations from the past 90 days across sources. The other pages concern policies, passwords and settings.

questions.stem: A team aggregates a non-authoritative source every hour during business hours. Which change BEST follows SailPoint's guidance?
choices: Aggregate daily, outside business hours
Aggregate only when the source owner asks
Aggregate every few minutes for fresher data
Disable optimization on every scheduled run
questions.answer: Aggregate daily, outside business hours
questions.explanation: Best practice is to aggregate as infrequently as the business allows, rarely more than daily for non-authoritative sources, and outside business hours. Unoptimized runs add load.

questions.stem: An admin explains correlation to a reviewer. Which description is BEST?
choices: Creating a new identity for every aggregated account
Grouping entitlements into access profiles automatically
Copying identity attributes onto every account on a source
Matching accounts to identities by attribute values
questions.answer: Matching accounts to identities by attribute values
questions.explanation: Correlation compares account attributes with identity attributes and assigns the account when they match. Creating identities is the job of authoritative sources.

questions.stem: When configuring account correlation, what operation does ISC apply between the identity attribute and the account attribute?
choices: Equals, which cannot be changed
Contains, or optionally Starts With
Greater Than, used for dates
Regex, defined per criteria
questions.answer: Equals, which cannot be changed
questions.explanation: Correlation criteria always use Equals. Partial matching is not available in the UI configuration.

questions.stem: A source has two correlation criteria: employee ID first, then email. What happens if the first criteria finds no match for an account?
choices: ISC creates a new identity for the account
ISC tries the next criteria in the listed order
The account is deleted from ISC
The account is immediately marked uncorrelated
questions.answer: ISC tries the next criteria in the listed order
questions.explanation: ISC correlates one attribute at a time in the configured order, and a match on any criteria assigns the account. Order matters, so the most reliable attribute should come first.

questions.stem: An admin wants to correlate on a custom identity attribute, but it does not appear in the Identity Attribute list. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The attribute is not configured as searchable for correlation
Custom identity attributes can never be used as correlation criteria
Delta aggregation is turned on
The source has no owner
questions.answer: The attribute is not configured as searchable for correlation
questions.explanation: Identity attributes must be searchable to appear in the list, and a limited number of extra ones can be made searchable through the API. Ownership and delta settings are unrelated.

questions.stem: A legacy app has account IDs that differ only by letter case. What does SailPoint documentation state about letter case during correlation?
choices: It is case-sensitive unless a transform converts both values
It is always case-sensitive, with no way to change it
It is case-insensitive, and ignoreCase can change this per source
It is case-sensitive for emails but not for IDs
questions.answer: It is case-insensitive, and ignoreCase can change this per source
questions.explanation: Documentation states that correlation is case insensitive and that the ignoreCase option in the Update Correlation Config API changes this per source. Community reports suggest some tenants default ignoreCase to false, so check the source's correlation config when IDs differ only by case.

questions.stem: No configured correlation criteria matches an account. What default logic does ISC still try?
choices: Matching the account to the source owner
Matching it to the newest identity in the tenant
Matching Account Name to the identity's name
Matching the account's email to the manager's email
questions.answer: Matching Account Name to the identity's name
questions.explanation: If configured criteria fail, ISC falls back to matching the Account Name attribute to the identity name, case-insensitively. This default is not configurable.

questions.stem: When should account correlation ideally be configured for a new source?
choices: After the first certification campaign
Only after every account is manually correlated
After the source has been reset twice
Before the first account aggregation
questions.answer: Before the first account aggregation
questions.explanation: Configuring correlation first means accounts link to identities as they are loaded. Changing it later requires an unoptimized aggregation.

questions.stem: What is an uncorrelated account in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: An account disabled on its source
An account on a source that has no source owner assigned yet
An account with no entitlements
A source account not linked to an authoritative identity
questions.answer: A source account not linked to an authoritative identity
questions.explanation: Uncorrelated accounts could not be matched to an identity, so they cannot be governed until resolved. Disabled or empty accounts may still be correlated.

questions.stem: After aggregating several sources, an admin wants one list of every uncorrelated account across the tenant. What should the admin generate?
choices: The Aggregation Activity list for the last 90 days
The account schema template
The Policy Violations export
The global Uncorrelated Accounts report
questions.answer: The global Uncorrelated Accounts report
questions.explanation: The global Uncorrelated Accounts report lists uncorrelated accounts and their sources. Aggregation Activity shows jobs, not unmatched accounts.

questions.stem: A few accounts on one source belong to known users but use misspelled IDs. Which manual method uses a file to link them?
choices: Create an SoD policy listing the accounts
Export the source accounts and reset the source
Download Correlation File, add userName values and upload the file
Download Account Schema, add the users and run a delta aggregation
questions.answer: Download Correlation File, add userName values and upload the file
questions.explanation: The correlation file lists uncorrelated accounts, and adding the identity's account name in userName links them. The schema template is for importing accounts.

questions.stem: An account was manually correlated, then its source data changed so it now matches another identity. What happens on the next aggregation?
choices: It moves to the newly matching identity on that aggregation
It becomes uncorrelated again
It is deleted from ISC
It stays with the identity it was manually linked to
questions.answer: It stays with the identity it was manually linked to
questions.explanation: Manual correlation creates a permanent link with manuallyCorrelated set to true, and even unoptimized aggregation does not remove it. The account must be removed or the flag changed.

questions.stem: An admin wants to correct one wrongly correlated account from the Accounts list. Which action should they use?
choices: Aggregate Account
Update Correlation on the account
Disable Account
Unlock Account
questions.answer: Update Correlation on the account
questions.explanation: Update Correlation lets the admin pick the correct identity for the account. Disable, unlock and aggregate change status or data, not ownership.

questions.stem: Many accounts on a source are uncorrelated because they belong to former employees. What is the BEST resolution?
choices: Create a new identity profile for former employees so they correlate
Remove the old accounts from the source system and aggregate again
Manually correlate them to the source owner
Disable correlation on the source
questions.answer: Remove the old accounts from the source system and aggregate again
questions.explanation: Accounts of people who left should be removed on the source, then a new aggregation clears them from ISC. Linking them to the owner would hide orphaned access.

questions.stem: Hundreds of accounts on a newly onboarded source are uncorrelated. What should the admin review FIRST?
choices: The VA cluster time zone
The SoD policy risk levels
The source's account correlation configuration
Each account's password policy
questions.answer: The source's account correlation configuration
questions.explanation: A large number of uncorrelated accounts points to correlation criteria that do not fit the data. Manual correlation suits only a small number.

questions.stem: Match each aggregation type to how it behaves.

pairs.match: Reads all records but skips unchanged accounts
Reprocesses every account and re-evaluates correlation
Loads only changes since the last run on supported sources
Loads the entitlement objects and their details

targets_extra: Pushes identity attribute changes out to the source
questions.explanation: Optimized is the default, unoptimized forces a full recheck, delta reads only changes, and entitlement aggregation loads the catalog. Pushing changes out is attribute sync, not aggregation.

questions.stem: Put the steps for manually correlating accounts with a file in order.
items: Open the source's Uncorrelated Accounts page
Add each identity's account name in the userName column
Check the Latest Manual Correlation status
questions.explanation: The file comes from the source, gets the identity names, and goes back through upload. The Latest Manual Correlation card shows whether the import had issues.

questions.stem: A team updated correlation criteria on a source that was already aggregated. Which TWO actions should the admin take to check the new criteria and apply them to accounts whose data has not changed?
choices: Enable account deletion with a low threshold
Add the accounts to an SoD policy list
Run another optimized aggregation from the UI
Run an aggregation with disableOptimization set to true
Use the correlation Test option to estimate the match rate first
answers: Run an aggregation with disableOptimization set to true
Use the correlation Test option to estimate the match rate first
questions.explanation: Testing shows whether the new criteria will match, and an unoptimized aggregation applies them to unchanged accounts. An optimized run skips those accounts.

questions.stem: An account was deleted from a target system last week, but it still appears in ISC after aggregations. Which source setting is MOST likely turned off?
choices: Delta Aggregation
Enable Account Deletion
Governance Group for Source Management
Enable Schedule
questions.answer: Enable Account Deletion
questions.explanation: Accounts missing from an aggregation are deleted from ISC only when Enable Account Deletion is selected on the source. Scheduling and delta settings control when and what is read.

questions.stem: With account deletion enabled, how does a full aggregation decide that an account should be deleted from ISC?
choices: The account has no entitlements left
The account has been disabled on the source for 30 days
The account is no longer returned by the source during the aggregation
The account's identity has moved to a new lifecycle state such as inactive
questions.answer: The account is no longer returned by the source during the aggregation
questions.explanation: Deletion during aggregation is driven by absence: an account not detected in the aggregation is removed from ISC. Disabled or empty accounts still exist on the source.

questions.stem: A Helpdesk user runs Aggregate Account on one account that was deleted on the source. What happens to the account in ISC?
choices: It is recreated on the source
It is deleted immediately from ISC
It stays unchanged, because only full aggregations process deletions
It is converted into an uncorrelated account until the next full aggregation
questions.answer: It stays unchanged, because only full aggregations process deletions
questions.explanation: If the account is not found during single-account aggregation, it stays as it is. Only full source aggregations process deletions.

questions.stem: Do the account deletion settings on a source apply to manual aggregations as well as scheduled ones?
choices: Only when delta aggregation is turned off
Yes, the same settings apply to both
No, only scheduled aggregations delete accounts
No, only manual aggregations delete accounts
questions.answer: Yes, the same settings apply to both
questions.explanation: Documentation notes that the deletion settings apply during both manual and scheduled aggregations. Delta settings are separate.

questions.stem: A flat file source's latest upload accidentally contained only half of the users. Which setting protects the remaining accounts from being deleted in ISC?
choices: The source's correlation criteria order
The source owner assignment
The deletion percentage threshold
The identity profile priority
questions.answer: The deletion percentage threshold
questions.explanation: The deletion threshold cancels an aggregation that would delete more accounts than allowed. Correlation order and profile priority do not stop deletions.

questions.stem: An admin removes an account in ISC with Remove Account, but the account still exists on the source. What happens at the next full aggregation?
choices: It is added again and treated as a new account
It is deleted from the source system
It stays removed permanently
It is blocked by the deletion threshold
questions.answer: It is added again and treated as a new account
questions.explanation: Remove Account clears the account from ISC only. Because it still exists on the source, the next full aggregation loads it again and correlation runs fresh.

questions.stem: An aggregation would delete more accounts than the source's Percentage of Deleted Accounts Allowed. What does ISC do?
choices: Deletes all accounts and emails the owner afterwards
Deletes only up to the allowed percentage
Cancels the aggregation and generates a warning
Pauses the aggregation until the owner approves
questions.answer: Cancels the aggregation and generates a warning
questions.explanation: Exceeding the threshold cancels the aggregation with a warning, so no partial deletion occurs. This guards against bad files or connector errors.

questions.stem: A source has only 10 accounts, and the deletion percentage is set very low so that it rounds to zero accounts. What is the risk?
choices: The aggregation is cancelled only if 100 % of accounts would be deleted
The threshold is ignored and replaced with 50 %
Every aggregation is cancelled, even when no accounts at all would be deleted
Accounts are never deleted, even individually
questions.answer: The aggregation is cancelled only if 100 % of accounts would be deleted
questions.explanation: If the percentage does not round to at least one account, only a 100 % deletion cancels the run. Admins should set a value that represents at least one account.

questions.stem: For a source with 10 accounts, which threshold setting does documentation suggest so that losing even one account cancels the aggregation?
choices: 100 %, which blocks every deletion
Exactly 1 %, which rounds to one account
At least 5 %, which rounds to one account
0 %, which disables deletions
questions.answer: At least 5 %, which rounds to one account
questions.explanation: On small sources the percentage rounds to whole accounts. Setting at least 5 % on 10 accounts rounds to 10 %, or one account.

questions.stem: A source owner asks why the deletion threshold matters for an HR authoritative source in particular. Which answer is BEST?
choices: Authoritative sources cannot be aggregated at all unless a threshold is configured
A bad feed could delete many authoritative accounts and their identities
The threshold decides which identity profile applies
The threshold controls how often HR is aggregated
questions.answer: A bad feed could delete many authoritative accounts and their identities
questions.explanation: Losing authoritative accounts can move or delete identities, so a threshold prevents a truncated feed from causing mass identity loss. It does not control scheduling or priority.

questions.stem: An aggregation was cancelled by the deletion threshold. Where can the admin see more detail about it?
choices: The identity profile mapping preview
The password policy settings
The SoD Policy Violations page, filtered by the policy's risk level
The Info icon on the run's status in Aggregation History
questions.answer: The Info icon on the run's status in Aggregation History
questions.explanation: Aggregation History shows status per run, and the Info icon gives details on warnings, errors and terminations. The other pages do not track aggregation outcomes.

questions.stem: After a threshold cancellation, the admin confirms that a large reorganisation really did remove many accounts. Which approach is MOST reasonable?
choices: Disable account deletion permanently
Raise the threshold for one run, then restore it
Delete the source and onboard it again
Reset the source and recreate its access profiles
questions.answer: Raise the threshold for one run, then restore it
questions.explanation: The Percentage of Deleted Accounts Allowed is an editable source setting that cancels any aggregation exceeding it, and the documentation offers no one-off override. Once the deletions are confirmed as genuine, a sensible judgement is to raise it for a single run and then restore it so the protection returns. Disabling deletion permanently, resets and re-onboarding are far more disruptive.

questions.stem: An employee's record is removed from HR, the authoritative source, and account deletion is enabled. The identity has no other authoritative account. What does ISC try to do?
choices: Move the identity into the default identity profile
Keep the identity active with its last attributes
Delete the identity's accounts on every source immediately
Delete the identity during the nightly job
questions.answer: Delete the identity during the nightly job
questions.explanation: Once the authoritative account is gone and no other authoritative source covers the identity, the system attempts deletion during the nightly job. It does not delete accounts on other systems.

questions.stem: Which condition blocks deletion of an identity whose authoritative account was removed?
choices: The identity owns a role, access profile, application or source
The identity's account was disabled on the HR source before it was removed
The identity has never signed in to ISC
The identity's lifecycle state is active
questions.answer: The identity owns a role, access profile, application or source
questions.explanation: Ownership of access objects is one of the blocking conditions, along with correlated accounts, open work items, being a manager and elevated user levels.

questions.stem: An identity could not be deleted because it still has correlated accounts on other sources. How does ISC keep it?
choices: As a hidden identity
As a new authoritative identity
As a governance group
As a protected admin identity
questions.answer: As a hidden identity
questions.explanation: Blocked identities remain as hidden identities. They lose their identity profile and do not appear on the Identities page.

questions.stem: What happens to accounts that stay attached to a hidden identity?
choices: They are treated as uncorrelated accounts
They are moved to the identity's manager
They are locked until a certification completes
They are deleted from their sources
questions.answer: They are treated as uncorrelated accounts
questions.explanation: Accounts on a hidden identity are treated as uncorrelated, and in an uncorrelated accounts certification they are grouped under a shared uncorrelated identity.

questions.stem: Why might an admin who leaves the company remain in ISC as a hidden identity after HR removes them?
choices: Elevated user levels such as Org Admin block identity deletion
Admins cannot be removed from HR feeds
Hidden identities are created automatically for every admin each night
Admin identities never have authoritative accounts
questions.answer: Elevated user levels such as Org Admin block identity deletion
questions.explanation: Elevated user levels such as role admin, org admin or helpdesk are a blocking condition. Removing those levels and other links lets deletion proceed.

questions.stem: Which statement about manager relationships and identity deletion is accurate?
choices: Manager relationships are ignored during deletion
Managers are deleted first, and their direct reports are deleted with them
Deleting a manager automatically deletes the reports
An identity designated as another identity's manager cannot be deleted
questions.answer: An identity designated as another identity's manager cannot be deleted
questions.explanation: Being someone's manager is one of the documented blocking conditions. The manager link must be updated before deletion can happen.

questions.stem: A misspelled email caused an account to correlate to the wrong person. The fix has been made on the source. Which action lets the account correlate correctly on the next aggregation?
choices: Delete Account
Disable Account
Unlock Account
Remove Account in ISC
questions.answer: Remove Account in ISC
questions.explanation: Remove Account takes the account out of ISC only, and the next aggregation treats it as new. Delete Account removes it from the source system.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between Remove Account and Delete Account in ISC?
choices: Remove affects the source system, while Delete affects only ISC
Remove affects only ISC, while Delete removes the account from the source system
Both delete the account on the source system, but Remove skips any approval step
Both affect only ISC, but Delete also clears entitlements
questions.answer: Remove affects only ISC, while Delete removes the account from the source system
questions.explanation: Remove Account clears ISC's copy, which returns on the next full aggregation. Delete Account sends a deletion to the source and may require approval.

questions.stem: An admin deletes an account, but it is recreated after the next identity refresh. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The deletion threshold was set too low
The account was never correlated
A role still assigned to the identity includes entitlements on that source
The source has delta aggregation enabled, so the deletion was never recorded
questions.answer: A role still assigned to the identity includes entitlements on that source
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends removing roles before deleting accounts, because an active role assignment provisions the account again on refresh.

questions.stem: Which sources allow an admin to use Delete Account?
choices: Any source that has a source owner
Only authoritative sources
Every flat file source
Direct connect sources that support account deletion
questions.answer: Direct connect sources that support account deletion
questions.explanation: Account deletion is available only on direct connect sources whose connectors support it. Flat file sources are read only.

questions.stem: A Delete Account request targets a Service Desk Integration source. What happens?
choices: A ticket is created to track the deletion
The request is rejected because SDIM sources are read only
The account is deleted directly by the connector
The account is removed from ISC only
questions.answer: A ticket is created to track the deletion
questions.explanation: For Service Desk Integration sources, a ticket tracks the deletion request in the service desk tool.

questions.stem: An admin changed a source's schema and wants to reload all its data without losing the source configuration. What should the admin do?
choices: Remove each account one at a time
Reset the source with the API, then run a full aggregation
Delete the source and create it again with the same configuration
Lower the deletion threshold
questions.answer: Reset the source with the API, then run a full aggregation
questions.explanation: A reset removes accounts and entitlements while keeping the configuration, and a full aggregation reloads them. Deleting the source loses its configuration.

questions.stem: Before resetting a source's entitlements, which side effect should the admin plan for?
choices: The source owner is cleared
Identity profiles that use the source are deleted
Its access profiles are deleted
Aggregation schedules are removed
questions.answer: Its access profiles are deleted
questions.explanation: Removing entitlements also removes the source's access profiles. Aggregation schedules are retained after a reset.

questions.stem: An admin tries to delete a source and sees a list of items connected to it. What must happen before deletion succeeds?
choices: Reset its data and remove its references from profiles, apps and transforms
Set the deletion threshold to 100 %
Assign a new source owner
Disable the source's virtual appliance cluster so nothing can reach the source
questions.answer: Reset its data and remove its references from profiles, apps and transforms
questions.explanation: A source in use cannot be deleted. Its data must be reset and references removed from identity profiles, access applications and transforms.

questions.stem: An admin wants to review all recent activity performed by or on one source. What is the QUICKEST place to start in Search?
choices: The identity profile mapping preview
The Policy Violations page filtered by level
The Identities list filtered by lifecycle state
The Source Activity suggested search
questions.answer: The Source Activity suggested search
questions.explanation: Search offers a Source Activity suggested search that can be narrowed to one source name. The other pages do not show source events.

questions.stem: Which search query BEST finds events where a source named HR Feed is the actor, target or source of an event?
choices: NOT _exists_:"HR Feed"
actor.name:"HR Feed" OR target.name:"HR Feed" OR attributes.sourceName:"HR Feed"
@accounts(source.name:"HR Feed")
source:"HR Feed" AND status:ACTIVE
questions.answer: actor.name:"HR Feed" OR target.name:"HR Feed" OR attributes.sourceName:"HR Feed"
questions.explanation: Documented guidance combines actor, target and attributes.sourceName to cover all events for one source. The @accounts query returns identities with accounts there, not events.

questions.stem: An admin wants to find account requests that failed and will not be retried. Which query fits?
choices: @accounts(disabled:true)
status:ERROR
NOT _exists_:manager
@accountRequests(result.status:failed)
questions.answer: @accountRequests(result.status:failed)
questions.explanation: Account activity searches use nested accountRequests results, and a failed status means the action will not be retried. status:ERROR finds identities in error.

questions.stem: In Search, an admin wants identities that are in an error state, for example because of correlation problems. Which query should they use?
choices: @accountRequests(result.status:failed)
type:error AND source:*
attributes.sourceName:ERROR
status:ERROR
questions.answer: status:ERROR
questions.explanation: Identities in error can be found with status:ERROR. Failed account requests are a different record type.

questions.stem: A provisioning audit shows a Create Account Failed event. In which Search category do such audit events appear?
choices: Events
Roles
Entitlements
Identities
questions.answer: Events
questions.explanation: Audit events such as failed account creations appear on the Events tab with normalized names. Identities, roles and entitlements are object categories.

questions.stem: An admin wants a weekly email of failed source events without logging in. What should they set up?
choices: An SoD policy schedule with subscribers
A subscription to a saved search
A password sync group
A source deletion threshold
questions.answer: A subscription to a saved search
questions.explanation: Saved searches can be subscribed to so results arrive by email on a schedule. SoD schedules report policy violations, not source events.

questions.stem: Where are notices about source errors displayed in ISC?
choices: Only in the source owner's Task Manager, as a separate work item for each error
Only in an SoD violation email
In System Components Status, the sources list and on the source itself
Only in the identity's Access tab
questions.answer: In System Components Status, the sources list and on the source itself
questions.explanation: Source errors appear in the System Components Status, the sources list and on the source page, and the home page summarizes errors and warnings over the last 7 days.

questions.stem: A source page shows Target system failing, and the VA cluster is healthy. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The flat file used the wrong template
The VA cluster serving the source is offline or still configuring after an update
Expired service credentials or a network path that cannot reach the source
The source has no owner assigned
questions.answer: Expired service credentials or a network path that cannot reach the source
questions.explanation: Target system failing means the VA works but the source may be unreachable, often because of credentials, hostnames or network routing. A failing VA shows a different banner.

questions.stem: A flat file source shows the banner Account file import failed. What should the admin do?
choices: Disable account deletion on the source
Restart the VA cluster that serves the source and then retry the upload
Verify the file uses the source's template and upload it again
Run an unoptimized aggregation using the API
questions.answer: Verify the file uses the source's template and upload it again
questions.explanation: This banner means an uploaded file did not import correctly, so the template and file must be checked before retrying. Flat file imports do not use a VA.

questions.stem: A new source shows Source config is incomplete, please add accounts. How should the admin interpret this?
choices: As a sign that correlation is misconfigured
As a critical VA failure that needs a case opened with SailPoint support
As an SoD conflict on the source
As an informational banner, solved by aggregating or uploading accounts
questions.answer: As an informational banner, solved by aggregating or uploading accounts
questions.explanation: This banner is not an error state; no accounts have been loaded yet. Running an aggregation or uploading a file clears it.

questions.stem: The team wants an email whenever a source enters an error state. What should the admin configure?
choices: The source's correlation criteria
System notifications for source health
A password policy on the source
A schedule on an SoD policy
questions.answer: System notifications for source health
questions.explanation: System health notifications can email admins when a source goes into error. Password, SoD and correlation settings do not send health alerts.

questions.stem: A source is Unhealthy, and Active Directory provisioning and password resets are failing. Which cause does documentation highlight?
choices: Lost connectivity between the source and IQService
The source's deletion threshold is too high
The Uncorrelated Accounts report has not been run
The identity profile has too many mappings
questions.answer: Lost connectivity between the source and IQService
questions.explanation: Losing IQService connectivity affects provisioning and password resets for sources that rely on it. Reports and thresholds do not affect connectivity.

questions.stem: Aggregations fail intermittently with Connection Reset errors on a supported source. Which configuration can make ISC retry them automatically?
choices: Enable delta aggregation on the source
Patch the retry connector attributes
Assign a governance group for source management
Increase the Percentage of Deleted Accounts Allowed
questions.answer: Patch the retry connector attributes
questions.explanation: Supported sources treat some errors as retryable, and admins can add errors and tune wait time and retry count by patching connector attributes. Deletion thresholds and delta do not retry.

questions.stem: Match each source status banner to its MOST likely cause.

pairs.match: The virtual appliance serving the source is down
The VA works, but credentials or network to the target fail
An uploaded file did not match the source template

pairs.item: Source config is incomplete, please add accounts
pairs.match: No accounts have been loaded yet

targets_extra: An SoD policy has items in only one list
questions.explanation: Each banner narrows the fault to the VA, the target, the file or missing data. SoD policy definitions do not produce source banners.

questions.stem: Put the steps for deleting a source that is still in use in order.
items: Select Connections on the source to review what depends on it
Reset the source and remove its identity profile, access app and transform references
Wait until no identity data is being processed in the tenant
Delete the source from the sources list or its configuration page
questions.explanation: Connections shows what depends on the source. Its data is reset and every reference removed, and because a source cannot be deleted while identity data is processing, the admin waits for processing to finish before deleting it.

questions.stem: An identity's only authoritative account was deleted, but the identity remains as a hidden identity. Which TWO conditions could have blocked its deletion?
choices: Its account was disabled before deletion
It owns an access profile
It was last aggregated more than a week ago
Its email address is blank
It has an active access request approval work item
answers: It has an active access request approval work item
questions.explanation: Owning access objects and having active work items both block identity deletion. Aggregation age, a blank email or a disabled account do not.
